title: Cut to a track
summary: See where a model cuts a picture with a fixed 30-second track and where it cuts against it.
originNote: Original task written for cross-model comparison of editing to music. Kitchen synthesizes the track and its cue sheet from a committed seeded generator (generator/track.mjs); subject and look are left to the model. The benchmark shape awaits owner acceptance.

setup.instructions: Read fixtures/brief.md and the supplied inputs under inputs/. If a skill layer is mounted at skill/, read skill/SKILL.md before planning; otherwise work from the brief alone. Kitchen supplies the same pinned toolchain (Node 22 or later, Python, a browser, FFmpeg and fonts) and compute profile to every compared model and layer. Before Ready, that toolchain must be pinned and smoked; this draft is not cookable.

turns.content: Read fixtures/brief.md and the supplied inputs, and any mounted skill. Make the picture for the supplied track and deliver the movie, edit decision list, live player, source, contact sheet and evidence. Make routine creative decisions yourself and iterate from rendered evidence.

checks.description: Check delivery files including edl.json, unchanged player, PNG signature, H.264/AAC, 1920 by 1080, 24fps, 720 frames, 30 seconds, complete decode, true peak at or below -0.1 dBTP and evidence structure.

Kitchen-side audio identity: the film's decoded soundtrack must match the supplied track's PCM within 20 ms, with every audible half-second correlated, nothing added in its silences, the same length, and its level within 0.5 dB. Light peak limiting is not detected.

Kitchen-side cut check: FFmpeg's scene-change measure finds the hard cuts in the picture and they must agree with edl.json within one frame. A declared cut needs a frame change of at least 0.3% and three times the quieter side's level; an undeclared change fails only when unmistakable (at least 6% and three times anything near it). Declared transitions are exempt, not confirmed. Changes in between are reported for tasting. Each cut's distance from the nearest supplied cue is reported, never gated.

Watch with sound, then muted. Where does the picture agree with the music and where does it argue, and do both feel chosen? What does it do with the four and a half seconds of silence, the one hit between beats, and the slow rise? Does the cutting keep a rhythm of its own with the sound off? Does the README's account match what you see?
